qa_pairs.question: How did the Application Binary Interface (ABI) change between GCC versions 4.9 and 5.1, and what is the recommended solution for linking issues with older binaries?
qa_pairs.answer: The transition from GCC version 4.9 to version 5.1 introduced a major change to its ABI. If linking to precompiled libraries built with the older ABI, users can address this by utilizing GCC's Dual ABI feature. This involves passing `-D_GLIBCXX_USE_CXX11_ABI=0` to GCC when using version 5.1 or higher to properly link with those legacy libraries. Alternatively, recompiling all source code, including all dependent libraries, with the same version of the compiler will prevent these issues.

qa_pairs.question: What options are recommended for users of Intel C/C++ compilers to ensure ANSI/ISO/IEEE standards-compliant floating-point support?
qa_pairs.answer: Users of Intel C/C++ compilers should consult the Intel man pages (e.g., `man icpc`) and are recommended to use one of two options: `-fp-model precise` or `-fp-model source`. These options ensure ANSI/ISO/IEEE standards-compliant floating-point support, as Intel compilers may otherwise default to using potentially unsafe optimizations for floating-point operations.
